seo.title: Calabash Grenada: Butler-Service Boutique Honeymoon 2026
seo.description: L'Anse aux Epines cove, butler per villa, intimate 30-suite boutique. Honest verdict, best room, 7-night Grenada itinerary, real cost.

content.verdict: Calabash Luxury Boutique Hotel is Grenada's most intimate property — a 30-suite, family-owned, butler-service boutique on the calm horseshoe cove of L'Anse aux Epines (locally pronounced "lance-o-peen") on the south coast. Owned by the Garbutt family for three generations, the property is built around eight acres of mature tropical gardens with the suites arranged in low whitewashed two-storey blocks facing the cove. Every suite gets a personal butler who delivers breakfast on the private balcony each morning. The cove itself is the secret weapon: a calm, mostly-private bay with no cruise-ship visibility and a small white-sand beach perfect for swimming and kayaking. Rhodes Restaurant (Gary Rhodes' Caribbean outpost when he was alive, now operated under his name with the same culinary direction) is genuinely the best fine-dining restaurant on Grenada and one of the best in the eastern Caribbean. Calabash is the choice for couples who want full butler-service Caribbean luxury at the scale of Anguilla's Quintessence — 30 suites, owner-on-property, every staff member knowing every guest — but on a leeward cove rather than a long Grand Anse stretch. The honeymoon atmosphere is dense and consistent.
content.best_room: The Calabash Pool Suites — eight of the thirty suites have private plunge pools on a wraparound terrace, with the breakfast butler bringing coffee and tropical fruit each morning at the requested time. Suite 1 (closest to the beach) and Suite 30 (the highest elevation with the broadest cove view) are the two most-requested honeymoon configurations. For couples not needing a private pool, the standard Suite category is still butler-serviced, has direct cove access via the garden paths, and runs at a significantly lower rate while preserving the full Calabash experience.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Arrival at L'Anse aux Epines
itinerary_7_nights.description: Direct from JFK or MIA to Maurice Bishop International (GND) in 4 hours, then a 6-minute transfer south to L'Anse aux Epines — Calabash is closer to the airport than any other property on the island. The butler meets arrivals at the suite with a chilled rum punch and unpacks the luggage. First dinner at Rhodes Restaurant — the seven-course tasting menu is the canonical introduction and includes Grenadian lobster, callaloo, and a nutmeg-infused dessert.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Cove Day & Spa
itinerary_7_nights.description: L'Anse aux Epines cove is the morning — Calabash has its own small beach with calm swimming water, complimentary kayaks, and snorkel gear. Lunch at the beachfront Beach Club restaurant (lobster salad, conch fritters). Afternoon at the Calabash Spa for the 90-minute Aromatic Spice Massage using locally-blended nutmeg and cinnamon oils. Sunset cocktails at the open-air bar above the cove.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Belmont Estate Cocoa Tour
itinerary_7_nights.description: The butler arranges a private driver for the 90-minute drive to Belmont Estate in St Patrick. Full cocoa-to-bar tour including the cocoa fermentation sheds, sun-drying boucan trays, and the Grenada Chocolate Company facility. Lunch at the estate's verandah buffet (oildown, callaloo, fresh juices), then a stop at the Pearl's spice market on the return drive for nutmeg, mace, and cinnamon to take home.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Underwater Sculpture Park
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive 20 minutes north to Grand Anse to board the boat for Molinere Bay's Underwater Sculpture Park — Jason deCaires Taylor's installations sit in 3-8m of clear water and snorkel access is straightforward. Three-hour trip with additional stops at Dragon Bay and Flamingo Bay reefs. Lunch back at Calabash on the cove, afternoon rest, dinner at Rhodes Restaurant for the second time (à-la-carte rather than tasting menu).

itinerary_7_nights.title: Annandale Falls & Grand Etang
itinerary_7_nights.description: Inland exploration of the volcanic interior — Annandale Falls (10-metre cascade) and Grand Etang National Park (crater lake at the island's centre surrounded by rainforest, with Mona monkeys descending to the trail). Lunch at the Grand Etang lookout restaurant, return via St George's port for an afternoon walk through the spice market and along the Carenage harbourfront.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Catamaran Day to Carriacou or Tobago Cays
itinerary_7_nights.description: Full-day private catamaran charter arranged by the Calabash concierge — typically heading north to Carriacou (Grenada's quiet sister island) or to the Tobago Cays in the southern Grenadines for the best snorkeling in the region. Lunch on board with grilled lobster and rum punches, snorkel stops at Sandy Island, return to L'Anse aux Epines by 5pm for sunset cocktails on the suite balcony.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Spa & Departure
itinerary_7_nights.description: Final morning split between the cove, a 90-minute spa treatment, and breakfast on the suite balcony delivered by the butler. Calabash is 6 minutes from Maurice Bishop International — the closest of any Grenada luxury property — so couples can enjoy a full late morning and noon checkout before transferring.

caveats: L'Anse aux Epines cove is calm and intimate but far smaller than Grand Anse — couples wanting a long beach walk should plan a day or two at Grand Anse 20 minutes away.
Hurricane risk July-October; the resort closes annually for a renovation window in September.
Calabash is family-owned with classic Caribbean styling — not minimalist or modern. Couples wanting the design-forward look should book Silversands.
Standard Suites are not directly on the beach; only the Pool Suites have the apex cove-front position.

faqs.question: Good for honeymooners?
faqs.answer: Calabash is one of the most consistently rated honeymoon hotels in the Caribbean — the 30-suite scale, butler service for every suite, the cove privacy, and Rhodes Restaurant on property create an exceptionally intimate honeymoon experience. The Garbutt family attention is the differentiator: every honeymoon couple is known by name and treated as such throughout the stay.

faqs.question: Best time to visit?
faqs.answer: December through May is the ideal dry-season window with cooling trade winds. February and March are the calmest months for cove swimming. May and early June offer excellent shoulder value before the July-October hurricane risk. November is the re-opening month with quieter rates and improving weather. Avoid September (closure).

faqs.question: Book in advance?
faqs.answer: The eight Pool Suites book 4-6 months ahead for high season; standard Suites have more flexibility. Christmas, Valentine's, and Easter sell out a year ahead. The butler-service standard means the property never overbooks, so confirmed reservations are honoured even if the configuration is at capacity.

faqs.question: Adults-only?
faqs.answer: Calabash accepts children over 12 in high season but is functionally a couples-and-honeymoon property — the 30-suite scale and butler-service model do not support young children. Honeymoon atmosphere is consistent year-round and the property is one of the most romantic configurations in the Caribbean.

faqs.question: Best room type?
faqs.answer: A Calabash Pool Suite (one of the eight) is the apex experience — private plunge pool, cove views, and the highest level of butler attention. Suite 1 and Suite 30 are the two most-requested honeymoon configurations. For lower budgets, the standard Suite category is still butler-serviced and has the full Calabash experience at significantly lower rate.

faqs.question: How to get there?
faqs.answer: Maurice Bishop International (GND) is 6 minutes from Calabash — closer than any other Grenada luxury property. Direct service operates from JFK (American, JetBlue), Miami (American), and London Gatwick (British Airways). European travellers without a direct usually connect via St Lucia (SLU) or Barbados (BGI). The butler team meets arrivals at the airport with a chilled drink.
